## Checks

Small checks used by the other scripts: that files exist, that required columns or keys are present, and that a step did not change the number of rows. Each stops with a message naming what is missing, never a data value.

```{r}
#| label: check-functions
#| eval: false
```

## Record corrections

Applies the corrections listed for one data source: each names a record by its identifier and sets one field to a new value. A correction that matches no record, or more than one, stops the run, so a correction can never be applied silently to the wrong record or skipped. The messages name the source and field, not the identifier.

```{r}
#| label: apply-record-corrections
#| eval: false
```

## Day jitter

Moves each day offset by its own random whole number of days, from minus to plus the given maximum. A shift that would carry an event across day 0 is applied in the opposite direction instead, so every event stays in its own period, matching how periods are assigned (after day 0 is post-intervention). The same happens to a shift that would move an event from before day 0 onto day 0 itself, where the timeline draws no line. The seed is set only inside the function, so the shifts are the same on every run and nothing else in the session is affected.

```{r}
#| label: jitter-days
#| eval: false
```

## Display labels

Turns a column into a factor whose levels keep their default order, with some shown under new names. The tables use it to print categories as the paper does without changing the data.

```{r}
#| label: relabel-levels
#| eval: false
```
